_comment: Watchlist for competitor outlier mining (/competitors/mine). Each week the miner pulls each channel's recent SHORTS, finds the ones that beat that channel's OWN median views (an outlier - a breakout, normalized per channel so a small channel is judged fairly against a giant one), and distills the transferable topic/angle patterns into competitor_signals.json, which the topic generator reads as inspiration. It NEVER copies titles. Edit this list freely: add a channel with either a channel_id (UC...) or a handle (@name) - at least one is required; the miner resolves and validates each at runtime and reports any it could not resolve. You can also override this whole list without a code edit via the COMPETITOR_CHANNELS env var (a comma-separated list of @handles/UC ids, set as a GitHub secret; applies on the next deploy). These channels were hand-verified on YouTube as faceless, SHORTS-NATIVE, single-fact / curiosity channels with UNIVERSAL (non-regional) content - the closest matches to this channel's format. Deliberately excluded: long-form fact/compilation channels (they post no Shorts) and region-specific news channels (e.g. India-news 'fact' channels, whose viral Shorts are local news, not reproducible universal facts).
